intro.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a dynamic React component that displays different content based on user conditions, such as showing a welcome message for logged-in users or a login prompt for guests. You'll learn conditional rendering, a fundamental React concept that allows components to display different UI elements based on the application's state or props. The core programming construct you'll master is the ternary operator (condition ? trueValue : falseValue), which provides a concise way to handle conditional logic directly within JSX. You'll work with React functional components, JSX syntax, and state management using the useState hook. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to create responsive user interfaces that adapt their content dynamically based on different conditions.
intro.usecase: Conditional rendering with ternary operators is essential for creating dynamic user interfaces that respond to user state and interactions. You'll see this pattern everywhere in modern web apps: showing login vs logout buttons based on authentication status, displaying loading spinners while data fetches, toggling between edit and view modes in forms, and showing different dashboard content based on user permissions. E-commerce sites use ternaries to show 'Add to Cart' vs 'Out of Stock' buttons, while social media platforms conditionally render follow/unfollow buttons and private/public content. This pattern is so fundamental that virtually every React component in production apps uses ternary operators to create responsive, state-driven user experiences.
